articles.title_orig: Taiwan flags ‘obvious’ threat from over 50 Chinese ships
articles.title_zh: Taiwan flags ‘obvious’ threat from over 50 Chinese ships
articles.content_orig:
Thursday, October 29, 2026 78° Today's Paper
By Ben Blanchard and Yimou Lee / Reuters
Today • Last updated
                                            9:12 a.m.
ANN WANG / REUTERS / OCT. 18, 2025
A Taiwan Coast Guard ship patrols near Dadan Island, Taiwan, last year. A senior Taiwan official said this week that China has over 50 navy and other official vessels operating from southern Japan down to Taiwan and off the Philippines.
TAIPEI, Taiwan >> China has over 50 navy and other official vessels operating in a wide swath of sea stretching from southern Japan down to Taiwan and off the Philippines, a senior Taiwan official said, calling the threat level “obvious.”
Taiwan, which China views as its own territory, is stepping up efforts to issue details and maps depicting locations where Chinese warships and Coast Guard vessels operate.
“We’re staying vigilant about their activities,” said Joseph Wu, the secretary-general of Taiwan’s National Security Council. “The simultaneous threat to Taiwan, Japan and the Philippines is obvious.”
Wednesday’s remarks accompanied a map he posted on X showing the locations of 53 ships, 34 of them navy warships, including the aircraft carrier Liaoning.
The carrier and its accompanying battle group were positioned to the east of the Philippines, with other formations off Taiwan’s east and southeast, along with three off the southern coast of Japan, according to the map.
Wu published a similar map on X in May.
Stay in touch with breaking news, as it happens, conveniently in your email inbox. It's FREE!
Today, Zhang Xiaogang, a Chinese defense ministry spokesperson, said the Liaoning carrier’s training in the western Pacific was an annual routine to test long-range, open-ocean combat capabilities and was not directed at any particular country.
The defense ministries of the Philippines and Japan did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
On Wednesday, Japan’s Defense Ministry said it had tracked three Chinese warships and a Coast Guard ship a day earlier as they passed through the narrow Osumi Strait off Kyushu island and into the Pacific.
This month, China’s Defense Ministry said the Liaoning was engaged in a routine training exercise not directed at any specific country.
China’s ties with both Japan and the Philippines have tanked in recent months. It has been upset by Japanese support for Taiwan, while embroiled in an increasingly bitter standoff with Manila in the South China Sea.
“We are not happy to see any attempt to project deterrence that could undermine peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific region,” Taiwan Defense Minister Wellington Koo told reporters at parliament in Taipei today.
A senior Taiwan security official briefed on the matter said one thing to watch would be whether the Liaoning carrier group continues north toward Japan after drills in the Philippine Sea.
“If it keeps moving north, that would suggest a stronger intent to put pressure on Japan’s defense posture,” the official said.
China has never renounced the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control, though it says it would prefer “peaceful reunification.”
U.S. Army forces in the Pacific have prepared the Indo-Pacific theatre under the assumption that China could move on Taiwan as early as next year, the U.S. military newspaper Stars and Stripes quoted Army Pacific commander Gen. Ronald Clark, as saying at a forum in Hawaii on Tuesday.
Taiwan was making efforts to build its own deterrence capabilities, Koo said when asked about Clark’s remarks.
“China has never abandoned the use of force to annex Taiwan,” he added.
China recognizes no separate sovereignty for Taiwan, whose government says only the island’s people can decide their future and that Beijing has no right to claim it.

articles.title_orig: Why Microsoft stock isn't getting crushed like Google stock after its earnings report
articles.title_zh: Why Microsoft stock isn't getting crushed like Google stock after its earnings report
articles.content_orig:
Amazon is slated to report third-quarter earnings results after the bell on Thursday.
Here's what analysts are expecting, according to LSEG:
Wall Street is also looking at other key revenue numbers:
Investors expect to see robust growth in Amazon's cloud segment. AWS sales are predicted to grow 38%, according to StreetAccount, compared with a 37% gain last quarter. It would mark AWS's fifth consecutive quarter of revenue acceleration.
That momentum isn't expected to slow down. CEO Andy Jassy said Amazon's cloud capacity is "largely sold out" for next year, and it's received significant commitments for 2028 as well.
"We always leave a certain amount for on demand and our inference service Bedrock or EC2, but largely sold out all the big chunks," Jassy said on an Andreessen Horowitz podcast last week. "A good chunk of '28 is sold out."
Wall Street will be listening for any commentary from Amazon executives around AI spending.
Last quarter, the company hiked its capital expenditure forecast for 2026 to $220 billion, up from $200 billion. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount expect Amazon's capex to creep up more than $280 billion in 2027.
Amazon has rushed to bring more data centers online to meet surging demand for AI computing power. The aggressive spending has eaten into the company's cash flow . In July, the company reported negative free cash flow of $7.6 billion for the trailing twelve months, compared with positive free cash flow of $18.2 billion one year earlier. It's expected to be cash flow negative in the current quarter, with an outflow of $9.9 billion, according to FactSet estimates.
Alphabet and Meta both reported negative free cash flow in their latest quarterly earnings reports. Microsoft said Wednesday its free cash flow declined 27% in the fiscal first quarter, but its cash flow remained positive, unlike its hyperscaler peers.
As Amazon shells out more on AI, it's steadily trimmed its headcount. The company has laid off more than 57,000 staffers since 2022, or roughly 16% of its corporate workforce. The job cuts have continued on a rolling basis this year via smaller rounds of layoffs.
The company on Wednesday laid off some staffers in its device software and services team to "operate more efficiently and better align with our product roadsmap," an Amazon spokesperson confirmed to CNBC. Fewer than 250 employees were let go as a result of the job cuts, the company said.
During the third quarter, Amazon made headlines when it blocked Meta 's Muse AI agent from shopping on its platform. The company said it was not given advance notice that Muse would access its webstore, and it never agreed to participate.
The move is in line with Amazon's broader stance on third-party agents accessing its site. Amazon has blocked dozens of external agents, including Perplexity , which the company sued last year over allegations that the startup concealed its AI shopping bots.
While it locks down its site from third-party agents, Amazon has increasingly invested in its own tools. In May, Amazon rebranded its Rufus AI shopping chatbot to Alexa for Shopping.
On Thursday, Amazon said more than 400 million shoppers have used the assistant, and the number of people using Alexa for Shopping's agentic features has "grown more than eight times since the start of the year."
The tool now has more than 100 shopping-related capabilities, the company said, including the ability to build gift lists, manage subscriptions and handle account changes.
As rivals Meta and OpenAI push deeper into AI shopping tools, analysts have said the services could pose a risk to Amazon's digital advertising business. Users are turning to services like Muse and ChatGPT to research products, or in some cases, handing off purchases to AI agents, which means they're bypassing sponsored ads on Amazon's site.
"We expect Amazon to eventually develop its own agentic shopping offering, with its proprietary purchase data and commerce infrastructure positioning it well," Deutsche Bank analysts wrote in a note last week. "The key question is whether Amazon can accommodate third-party agents on terms that preserve attractive monetization."

articles.title_orig: 'Operation Supercharge': Japan and U.S. agree to develop Japanese missile facility
articles.title_zh: 'Operation Supercharge': Japan and U.S. agree to develop Japanese missile facility
articles.content_orig:
From left, Philippines Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro, Australia Defense Minister Richard Marles, Japan Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and U.S.Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth prepare to leave after posing for pictures before holding a Quadrilateral Meeting on the sidelines of the 20th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Defence Ministers' Meeting (ADMM) and 13th ADMM-Plus Meetings in Cebu, Philippines, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. Rolex Dela Pena/Pool EPA via AP hide caption
CEBU, Philippines — The United States and Japan have agreed to establish a Japanese facility for the joint production of advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles, the Japanese defense chief said.
It is the latest move by the allies, which have repeatedly expressed alarm over China's growing assertiveness in Asia.
Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi made the announcement in a news conference Wednesday night in the central Philippine province of Cebu, where he met U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on the sidelines of an annual meeting of Southeast Asian defense chiefs and their major Asian and Western counterparts.
Koizumi raised concern Thursday about China's increasing naval activity in southwestern Japan. He said that three Chinese destroyers and a coast guard ship together crossed the Osumi Strait south of the southern main island of Kyushu and headed east to the Pacific Ocean this week. It was the first such fleet configuration his ministry has spotted, he said.
Koizumi said he cited the incident as "an example illustrating the challenging security environment in the region" in his remark at a session Thursday. His ministry will keep watching the Chinese activity with high level of interest, he said. Japan has been accelerating military buildup in southwestern Japan to deter China.
The annual meetings aim to avert a major regional conflict and strengthen defense cooperation. On the sidelines of the meetings, however, the U.S. and China and their allies have often traded criticisms.
The missiles that will be produced as part of a joint effort called "Operation Supercharge" are essential for the F-35 fighter jets, Koizumi said. The two sides agreed to build a final assembly and inspection plant for the Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile, or AMRAAM, in Japan, he said. The U.S.-made F-35s are one of the world's most advanced aircraft and are also used by the Japanese military.
During his brief meeting with Hegseth in Cebu, Koizumi said he "shared a sense of crisis … regarding the increasingly severe regional situation and we agreed to strengthen the deterrence and response capabilities of the Japan-U.S. alliance with greater speed and intensity than ever before."
"We reaffirmed the importance of a free and open international order based on the rule of law, which rejects any attempts to unilaterally alter the status quo through the use of force, coercion or other means," Koizumi said.
Hegseth renewed the Trump administration's repeated assurances of commitment to help deter aggression in the region in a separate meeting on Wednesday with ASEAN defense ministers, who were led by the host, Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. Like Koizumi, Hegseth did not mention China by name in expressing his security concerns in the region.
"The approach we're taking, we describe as strong, quiet and clear," Hegseth told the ASEAN defense chiefs. "Strong enough to deter coercion and aggression, quiet enough to avoid needless escalation or public theatrics to let our actions speak for themselves."
His message is "clear enough that our friends, our partners and potential adversaries understand precisely where the United States stands and that we will defend our interests and the interests of our allies and partners," Hegseth said.
Hegseth has assured the Philippines, the oldest treaty ally of Washington in Asia, that the Trump administration will build a robust deterrence against China's increasingly aggressive actions in the disputed South China Sea. Beijing claims the busy waterway, a key global trade route, virtually in its entirety.
Australian Defense Minister Richard Marles said his country's forces, along with allies like the U.S., will press on with efforts to defend the rule of law despite China's increasing assertiveness, including in the South China Sea. Australia protested last year after a Chinese J-16 fighter aircraft released flares and passed within 30 meters (100 feet) of an Australian P-8 Poseidon surveillance jet over the disputed waters.
"That doesn't deter us from doing what we need to do and that's essentially asserting the rules-based order here in the end of the Pacific," Marles told The Associated Press in Cebu on Wednesday. "Freedom of navigation on the high seas is profoundly important for Australia."
The Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei, all ASEAN member states, along with Taiwan, also have overlapping claims in the South China Sea. Confrontations have particularly escalated between Chinese and Philippine coast guard and navy vessels in disputed shoals and outlying waters.
Washington has warned that it's obligated to defend the Philippines if Filipino forces, ships and aircraft come under an armed attack, including in the South China Sea.
Beijing and Tokyo have a separate dispute over tiny Japanese-controlled islands in the East China Sea, with both sides often accusing the other of infringing on their maritime territory.

articles.title_orig: Israelis await final election results as claim of foreign interference emerges
articles.title_zh: Israelis await final election results as claim of foreign interference emerges
articles.content_orig:
Netanyahu’s claim of interference in election also dismissed by Israeli police and opposition parties
Israel’s choice: Netanyahu remaining in power or a Palestinian-backed coalition
Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesman rejected accusations “made by certain Israeli politicians and their contacts in the media” that his country had interfered in the Israeli elections.
“We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome,” Majed al-Ansari said on X.
“They accuse Qatar of buying off Benjamin Netanyahu , the Israeli political left and now, in this latest campaign, the Arab vote... These accusations are ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure.”
That’s all from me, Tom Ambrose, and from the Israel election results live blog for today.
Here is a round-up of today’s headlines:
Benjamin Netanyahu has been accused of using smear tactics to cling to power, after he claimed that Arab Israeli parties had used foreign backing to “steal” Tuesday’s election, in which the prime minister’s coalition lost its parliamentary majority. Netanyahu and his allies called on the internal security service, Shin Bet, to investigate alleged vote buying and other irregularities in Palestinian communities in Israel , supposedly funded by foreign money.
Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the main opposition bloc, accused the prime minister and his Likud party of trying to derail the election results. “It’s already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election,” Eisenkot said in a video message.
Netanyahu’s allegations were quickly disowned by a range of government officials, including police officers and members of the election committee. He was also rebuked by the president for “tarnishing an entire community”. On Wednesday night, the prime minister posted a statement by Likud online which described the claimed violations as “an attack on democracy whose purpose is to lead to a foreign takeover of the Knesset, the Islamisation of Israel, and the overthrow of rightwing rule”.
Opposition leaders lambasted the claims of Netanyahu, 77, who has run Israel for 19 of the past 30 years. Yousef Jabareen, the Joint List leader, accused the prime minister of incitement. “Netanyahu was defeated at the ballot box,” Jabareen said, adding that he “refuses to come to terms with the fact that the Arab public voted and decided”.
Ahmad Tibi, one of the leaders of the Joint List party, said Benjamin Netanyahu was on an orchestrated, toxic campaign meant to undermine the election results. “This entire campaign is directed against Eisenkot, to prevent him, intimidate and scare him off forming a government that relies on external support from the Joint List or Ra’am,” Tibi told Reuters.
Meanwhile, Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesman rejected accusations “made by certain Israeli politicians and their contacts in the media” that his country had interfered in the Israeli elections. “We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome,” Majed al-Ansari said on X.
Iran attempted to interfere in the Israeli election this week and will try to disrupt the US midterm elections next week, the Telegraph reports. “We have been looking into ways to recruit agents in both the American and Israeli regimes’ election processes,” one official said, adding that “powerful cyber groups have also been established to hack their election systems”.
The Israeli newspaper Haaretz has reported that, with 97% of votes counted, the balance between the political blocs remains unchanged. Netanyahu’s coalition remains at 53 seats and Eisenkot’s bloc at 48. Parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel hold 19 seats. The final tally of absentee ballots is not expected to significantly shift the results, with no grouping managing to reach the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset.
Mahmoud Abbas, the president of the Palestinian Authority, expressed hope that the Israeli election would pave the way for renewed peace talks. “For many years now, we have been extending a hand to the Israeli side in order to achieve peace with them, so that Israel and Palestine may live in security, stability and peace,” Abbas said during a meeting with Cypriot president Nikos Christodoulides in Nicosia.
The Israeli president, Isaac Herzog, has come to the defence of Palestinian voters, as he urged political leaders against “tarnishing an entire community that sought to exercise its right to vote”. He said Shin Bet and the country’s central elections committee would investigate allegations of foreign interference “throughly”.
The central elections committee’s acting director general, Dean Livne, said there was “no basis for claims of systematic violations of election integrity”. The Israeli police also dismissed the claims, according to comments reported in Hebrew-language media, with one source quoted as saying: “Election day passed with very few irregular incidents.”
Israel’s chief opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot has warned that prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu was working to delegitimise election results with his allegations of malfeasance by parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel that performed well.
“It’s already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election,” Eisenkot said in a video message, referring to the prime minister’s right-wing party.
Supreme Court justice Noam Sohlberg, a conservative who heads the Central Elections Committee, requested an investigation by the Shin Bet security service into allegations that Ra’am received money from Qatar .
“The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Netanyahu’s Likud party said.
Ra’am chief Mansour Abbas said his party had “no connection whatsoever to the affair” and welcomed an investigation.
Iran attempted to interfere in the Israeli election this week and will try to disrupt the US midterm elections next week, the Telegraph reports.
“We have been looking into ways to recruit agents in both the American and Israeli regimes’ election processes,” one official said, adding that “powerful cyber groups have also been established to hack their election systems”.
Meanwhile, another official described it as an extension of its war with the US and Israel.
“War does not just mean missiles and guns when we are under their blockade,” he said. “It also means we are prepared to disrupt their elections, their banking, their travel and all their ordinary systems. We are not in favour of any candidate anywhere, but we would like to see a divided America and a divided Israel.”
Ahmad Tibi , one of the leaders of the Joint List party, said Benjamin Netanyahu was on an orchestrated, toxic campaign meant to undermine the election results.
“This entire campaign is directed against Eisenkot, to prevent him, intimidate and scare him off forming a government that relies on external support from the Joint List or Ra’am,” Tibi told Reuters.
During and after Tuesday’s election, Netanyahu and his allies warned against rising Arab turnout and his right-wing Likud party issued statements accusing the parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel of “stealing the vote.“
It demanded police and the Shin Bet domestic intelligence service investigate incidents of suspected election bribery and intimidation at ballot stations. It said it possessed evidence of such activity but has not presented it to the ‌public.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia's relationship with China just got even more complicated as report says Jensen Huang was target of spy plot
articles.title_zh: Nvidia's relationship with China just got even more complicated as report says Jensen Huang was target of spy plot
articles.content_orig:
An Nvidia spokesperson on Thursday pushed back on a New York Times report that detailed American intelligence agencies surveilling a person close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang because they thought she could be a Chinese intelligence asset.
According to the Times report , which cited people briefed on intelligence surveillance, Alice Huang, who is linked to the Singapore-based cloud Megaspeed, developed a close relationship with Nvidia's Jensen Huang.
Intelligence agencies worried that she was a spy, helping the Chinese government gain information from Nvidia and Jensen Huang, and fretted that Nvidia's CEO had access to President Donald Trump.
The Nvidia spokesperson pushed back on the story in a statement to CNBC, saying that Singapore-based Megaspeed is another one of the company's regional cloud customers, and that Jensen Huang's interactions with its officials are not unusual, because he speaks with thousands of customers every year.
The spokesperson added that customers don't get access to Nvidia trade secrets or relevant national security information.
The report also alleged that Megaspeed was previously suspected of helping companies evade U.S. export controls on Nvidia's AI chips, which aren't allowed to be shipped to China.
Nvidia said that Megaspeed had already been investigated for evading export controls.
"The diversion allegations against this regional cloud were thoroughly investigated and debunked last year," the spokesperson said in a statement.
Nvidia implied that the U.S. government had not briefed Nvidia on Alice Huang.
"We're confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know," the spokesperson said.
Nvidia has had to walk a tightrope in Washington as its AI chips have become a powerful tool for all AI developers and a bargaining chip in economic competition with China.
Politicians and analysts say that Nvidia's AI chips could be used to create Chinese military AI models, or commercial AI models that could compete and eventually surpass American technology.
As AI has become more important to the government, Nvidia's Huang has befriended Trump and has given pro-American speeches about building U.S. AI infrastructure.
Huang has appeared with Trump at state dinners, AI summits, and international trips, all while pushing for certain Nvidia chips to get a green light to be shipped to China.
Earlier this year the U.S. government cleared Nvidia's H200 chip to be shipped to China, but Chinese regulators prevented their imports. H200s are Nvidia's Hopper generation chip, not the current faster Blackwell generation currently used by American AI developers.
The Nvidia spokesperson said the Chinese government is not looking for Nvidia products from regional clouds like Megaspeed.
"Instead, the PRC government blocked U.S. AI chips, protecting its own industry and resulting in the largest write-offs in U.S. tech history," the Nvidia spokesperson said. Last year, Nvidia wrote off about $4.5 billion in Chinese-tuned AI chips.

articles.title_orig: China's Communist Party seeks to tighten discipline
articles.title_zh: China's Communist Party seeks to tighten discipline
articles.content_orig:
Chinese President Xi Jinping, center left and Zhang Shengmin, Vice Chairman of the Central Military Commission second from right attend a ceremony in honor of fallen national heroes at the Monument to the People's Heroes to mark Martyrs' Day at Tiananmen Square in Beijing, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026. Ng Han Guan/AP hide caption
BANGKOK — China's top leaders on Thursday elevated the only remaining general on the commission that oversees the country's military to the Politburo, the top governing body of the Communist Party.
The leaders also adopted a resolution on strengthening self-governance, discipline and anti-corruption in the party, as they seek to extend their grip on power.
During a four-day closed-door meeting, top Communist Party leaders deliberated on and adopted resolutions that will guide the party in the coming years. The meeting comes about a year before President Xi Jinping is widely expected to secure his fourth five-year term as the party's leader.
The party elected Gen. Zhang Shengmin, who currently serves as vice chairman of the Central Military Commission, to the Politburo. Xi had earlier purged two of China's top generals, leaving Zhang as the commission's only member besides Xi himself. It also left the Politburo without any representatives from the People's Liberation Army.
Zhang also holds a position overseeing internal discipline for the military, serving as deputy secretary of the CMC Commission for Discipline Inspection.
The party said in a summary of the resolution that the tasks facing it were "increasingly arduous," such as "uniting and leading the people to safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests."
It said it must step up its self-governance, which involves rooting out corruption and maintaining ideological purity.
The party should, "with an eye on enhancing its long-term governance capacity, maintain its progressive nature and purity, and its close, flesh-and-blood ties with the people," according to a summary of the resolution from the official Xinhua News Agency.
Xi has championed anti-corruption since coming to power in 2012, and has sustained a crackdown on officials for more than a decade. However, analysts say the focus now also includes underperforming officials.
Party members also reviewed the earlier purges of top members and military officials, confirming the personnel changes.
The plenum meeting revealed wider-than-expected purges, according to analysis by Neil Thomas, a senior fellow at Asia Policy who studies Chinese politics. He calculated an attendance rate of 74 percent, the lowest since the times of former leader Mao Zedong, who ran political purges regularly.

articles.title_orig: After losing his majority, Netanyahu tries to delegitimize election results
articles.title_zh: After losing his majority, Netanyahu tries to delegitimize election results
articles.content_orig:
This live blog is now closed – you can read the latest elections news here
This live blog is now closed – you can read the latest news on the elections here .
You can also read this analysis from our Middle East correspondent , Emma Graham-Harrison, who has outlined the options available to Benjamin Netanyahu in the light of Tuesday’s election results.
Israel’s future hangs in the balance as it has become clear that Benjamin Netanyahu has lost his governing majority . His political fate now depends on whether opposition Jewish parties are prepared to forge a common front with Palestinian parties , whose support surged in Tuesday’s historic elections. Indeed, Gadi Eisenkot and his allies face a clear choice: either make a pact with Arab Israeli parties heading for a record result of 19 seats, or hand Netanyahu a political lifeline in the form of new elections or a unity government.
Yair Golan, the leader of the centre-left Democrats, a junior partner in Eisenkot’s bloc, has told Israeli media that he will meet with three leaders tomorrow for coalition talks. According to the Times of Israel, they will be Eisenkot, the leading opposition candidate and chair of the Yashar party, and Yair Lapid, the number-two in the opposition B’Yachad party. This would mark the official start of coalition talks, and Golan has been the only opposition leader so far backing working with the parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel.
Israel’s Central Elections Committee said it had received the Likud party’s complaint alleging that Arab parties had compromised election integrity and would examine the claims as part of its routine post-election review. Netanyahu’s party responded to partial election results showing Arab-led parties could play a king-making rol e in forming a new government by accusing them – without evidence – of “stealing” the election and demanding that the police and Shin Bet security service investigate the allegations.
UN rights chief Volker Turk has said that he hopes the next Israeli government will “change course massively” and respect international law . “The message is: don’t continue the current course of warfare where you think you are above international law, because I think that’s what we have frankly seen in the current environment,” Turk told reporters in New York. He added: “Israel has its obligations under international law, international humanitarian law, international human rights law, and they need to respect them, and I hope that the next government will do precisely that and change course massively.”
Hours before the final results from Israel’s elections were in, several things were clear. Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right coalition had lost its mandate, and the opposition had a firm majority .
But most of Israel ’s Jewish opposition ruled out governing with Palestinian-led parties , in the course of a racist election campaign in which Netanyahu painted Palestinian citizens as an enemy inside the state.
The self-imposed ban on a broader opposition alliance , if it holds, offers Netanyahu the prospect of turning his defeat into another term in office – or at least a prolonged mandate as caretaker prime minister and perhaps another round of elections.
This confected barrier to unseating Netanyahu became the focus of Israeli media and analysts. “No Clear Government” announced the newspaper Israel Hayom. “Road to Unity Government Has Been Paved”, read an article on Channel 12.
Yair Golan , leader of the centre-left Democrats , attacked that framing. “ Netanyahu lost. I know how to count ,” he said in a statement calling for a government with Palestinians, who make up about 20% of Israel’s population.
double quotation mark We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes. We have a majority. We have a responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a change government in partnership with Arab citizens of Israel.
Other Israelis were even more direct. “ If you stop being racist two amazing things will happen to you ,” musician Yali Sobol wrote in a Facebook post. “ First, you will stop being racist. Second, you will discover you have won .”
While Palestinian-led parties do not describe themselves as Zionist, neither do some of the ultra-Orthodox groups who are a key part of Netanyahu’s current coalition.
A survey taken as polls closed on election day showed that a clear majority of opposition voters supported forming a government with the Palestinian-led Ra’am in order to unseat Netanyahu, political psychology researcher Eran Halperin said .
But opposition leaders were silent on Wednesday, as they apparently tried to balance their desire to unseat Netanyahu with promises against working with Palestinians.
Former general Gadi Eisenkot , who leads the biggest opposition party, has not directly ruled out governing with Palestinians but laid out conditions that made it politically impossible for them to join a coalition.
Palestinians have been clearer about their priorities. “ We are ready and prepared to pave the way for the ousting of the Netanyahu government ,” Yousef Jabareen , leader of the larger Joint List , said on Wednesday . “ The change comes through Jewish-Arab partnership. ”
For Palestinian citizens facing surging crime, discrimination and home demolitions inside Israel and watching family and friends endure ethnic cleansing in the occupied West Bank and a war of annihilation in Gaza, that was viscerally true, and they came out in record numbers.
Israel describes itself as a Jewish and democratic state. If the representatives of Palestinians are now effectively excluded from government because of their race, Netanyahu will have turned that promise into more of a choice – between a Jewish future or a democratic one.
Israel ’s Central Elections Committee has announced that the distribution of Knesset seats remains unchanged after 88.62% of the votes cast at polling stations across the country have now been counted .
The pro-Netanyahu bloc remains at 53 seats, while the opposition has 67, split between 48 for the Jewish-led parties and 19 for the Arab-led parties.
Further, the committee estimates that the total number of “double envelope” absentee ballots will be between 430,000 and 480,000. These are cast at special voting sites including military bases, prisons, and hospitals, and by diplomats, and have yet to be tallied.
Counting of those ballots is expected to begin at around 1am local time, and to conclude by Thursday evening , according to a committee spokesperson.
This live blog is now closed – you can read the latest news on the elections here .
You can also read this analysis from our Middle East correspondent , Emma Graham-Harrison, who has outlined the options available to Benjamin Netanyahu in the light of Tuesday’s election results.
Israel’s future hangs in the balance as it has become clear that Benjamin Netanyahu has lost his governing majority . His political fate now depends on whether opposition Jewish parties are prepared to forge a common front with Palestinian parties , whose support surged in Tuesday’s historic elections. Indeed, Gadi Eisenkot and his allies face a clear choice: either make a pact with Arab Israeli parties heading for a record result of 19 seats, or hand Netanyahu a political lifeline in the form of new elections or a unity government.
Yair Golan, the leader of the centre-left Democrats, a junior partner in Eisenkot’s bloc, has told Israeli media that he will meet with three leaders tomorrow for coalition talks. According to the Times of Israel, they will be Eisenkot, the leading opposition candidate and chair of the Yashar party, and Yair Lapid, the number-two in the opposition B’Yachad party. This would mark the official start of coalition talks, and Golan has been the only opposition leader so far backing working with the parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel.

articles.title_orig: Robust consumer spending, AI-related investment power US economy in third quarter
articles.title_zh: Robust consumer spending, AI-related investment power US economy in third quarter
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Driven by strong consumer spending and a surge in artificial intelligence investments, the U.S. economy expanded at a healthy 3.4% annualized pace between July and September, accelerating from the second quarter.
Figures released Thursday by the Commerce Department show that third-quarter gross domestic product—measuring total output across goods and services—outpaced the 2.2% growth recorded from April through June. Household spending increased at a swift 3.8% rate while business investment climbed sharply amid the boom in AI technology.
The performance demonstrates the ongoing resilience of the world’s largest economy, despite higher energy costs brought on by fighting with Iran. Growth surpassed expectations, topping the 3% expansion projected by forecasters in a survey by data firm FactSet.
Commercial investment, excluding housing, rose 12.7% as growth was lifted by AI spending. Capital outlays on information processing equipment jumped 37.4%, software rose 9.6%, and research and development increased 7.5%. Conversely, residential investment, constrained by high mortgage rates, fell 3.3%, marking its sixth decline in the last seven quarters.
Thursday’s report represents the first of three Commerce Department estimates regarding third-quarter GDP growth.
Inflation data was also released on Thursday. An inflation gauge closely monitored by the Federal Reserve accelerated last month, showing that prices remain elevated less than a week before midterm elections in which affordability concerns have become a central issue.
Consumer prices rose 3.6% in September from a year earlier, the Commerce Department said Thursday, up from 3.4% in August. On a monthly basis, prices climbed 0.5%, up from 0.3% in August and the highest figure since May.
Annual inflation has worsened since the Iran war caused spikes in oil and gas prices. U.S. oil prices still top $100 a barrel, up from less than $70 before the war. Polls show that the rise in inflation has soured most voters on the economy and President Donald Trump's handling of rising costs. Trump campaigned in 2024 on lowering prices, including bringing the cost of gas below $2 a gallon. It currently averages about $4.25 a gallon nationwide.
Excluding the volatile energy and food categories, inflation also picked up. It increased 3.1% from a year ago in September, up from 3% in August. And from August to September, core prices rose 0.3%, the same as the previous month.
The reports come a day after the Federal Reserve, the agency tasked with combatting inflation, left its key interest rate unchanged. With inflation above the Fed's 2% target and the economy charging ahead, the central bank will remain under pressure to raise rates at its next meeting in December.
Thursday's inflation data comes from the personal consumption expenditures price index, which typically echoes the better-known consumer price index published earlier this month. The Fed more closely monitors the PCE index because it puts less weight on housing prices and allows for changes in consumers' shopping habits.

articles.title_orig: At least 14 people killed in Russian attack on Dnipro train station
articles.title_zh: At least 14 people killed in Russian attack on Dnipro train station
articles.content_orig:
The site of the drone strike has been sealed off, as Ukrainian authorities continue their investigation
At least 14 people have been killed after a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro, local officials have said.
Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 14 others were wounded in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy.
Ukraine's state railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, said a passenger train headed for the southern city of Zaporizhzhia was at one of the platforms in Dnipro when the drone hit.
Russia's military has not publicly commented. It has repeatedly hit Ukraine's large railway network, but Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians.
In Dnipro, an elevated threat level was announced ahead of Thursday's strike, according to the railway operator chief, Oleksandr Pertsovsky.
"But unfortunately there were still a large number of people on the platform" when the drone struck, he said.
Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov said the incident was a tragedy, adding that a drone hit an electric civilian train.
Pictures from the Ukrainian rescue services show a large hole in a platform that is strewn with blurred-out bodies, near a blast-damaged train with smashed windows.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said "the Russians used a drone to attack a platform where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing."
He called for further US, European and G7 sanctions on Russia and repeated his criticism of a controversial deal that was struck earlier this month between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, which eased some sanctions on Moscow, allowing the US to import Russian diesel.
Elsewhere in Ukraine, two girls aged 15 were killed in a Russian missile attack on the centre of Chernihiv city, in the north of the country, regional head Vyacheslav Chaus said. At least 25 others, including four children, were injured, he added.
A day of mourning has been declared for Chernihiv and Dnipro on Friday.
In the city of Kremenchuk, in the central Poltava region, three people were killed and 28 injured in a Russian drone attack that hit residential buildings and a school, regional head Vitaliy Diakivnych said.
At least 25 people were injured in the Russian strike on Kremenchuk, local officials said
The latest Russian strikes came during efforts to uphold a fragile ceasefire in the besieged city of Oleshky, which has been under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have been trapped without food, water, medicine and electricity for years.
Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, wrote on Telegram that the truce was holding into a third day.
Meanwhile, the Kremlin has condemned Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow whilst the city hosts the Russia-Africa Summit, the Tass news agency has reported. The two-day event is attended by African leaders and government delegations from 48 countries.
The mayor of Moscow said 613 Ukrainian drones were launched overnight towards the region, most of which were shot down during their flight.
Russia's defence ministry has always denied targeting Ukrainian civilians and says its attacks on railways target the infrastructure used to transport military personnel and equipment.
However, the dangers to passengers are very real, and attacks on Ukraine's train infrastructure have risen sharply.
Of the 521 locomotives hit since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, almost 60% have been hit this year, according to statistics released by Ukrzaliznytsia supplied to AFP news agency.
Overall attacks on railway facilities have risen from 1,206 in 2025 to 1,700 so far this year.
There appears to have been a wider assault on Ukraine's infrastructure in recent weeks, with two bridges attacked in the capital Kyiv, and a metro train hit during one of the strikes.

articles.title_orig: Christine Lagarde to Step Down as Chief of European Central Bank
articles.title_zh: Christine Lagarde to Step Down as Chief of European Central Bank
articles.content_orig:
European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said on Thursday she had decided to step down eight months before her term was due to expire so that she can speak more freely on issues beyond monetary policy.
Lagarde, 70, has led the ECB since November 2019 and previously headed the International Monetary Fund. Her term would otherwise have run until October 2027.
“There is never a good time to leave,” Lagarde told a press conference. “But it’s embedded in the governance of the ECB that presidents, board members have to leave because they cannot be up for renewal.”
Lagarde said the decision to leave early was driven by a wish to engage on issues outside the ECB’s mandate.
“I want to have the freedom of speech, the freedom of expression and the freedom to engage on matters that are not monetary policy matters,” she said.
She noted that ECB officials are bound by strict rules of neutrality: “We have an obligation of neutrality, we comment on the situation with the focus on monetary policy,” Lagarde said, adding that the mandate is “the price we pay for being independent.”
Lagarde said she no longer felt comfortable staying silent on broader global issues. “I’m interested in the truth, and I see the truth being very often damaged, contradicted by misrepresentation,” she said, without elaborating.
Drawing on more than two decades in international economic and financial roles, Lagarde said she believed she had something to contribute beyond central banking. “There are things that I can say — whether people will listen or not is another story. But I feel that I should say those things and I cannot do so in my current position,” she said.
Lagarde sought to reassure markets and staff that her early departure would not disrupt the central bank’s operations. “A process has already started to identify my successor,” she said, adding there were “plenty of excellent candidates — much better than me, actually.”
She dismissed concerns about continuity. “Don’t worry about decision making in limbo — no, absolutely not,” Lagarde said. “The institution is solid, strong, like a rock, and it will continue being so.”

Eli Lilly (LLY) shares have been a major beneficiary as overspending and valuation concerns have made investors rotate out of artificial intelligence (AI) stocks in the trailing six months. But that benefit is likely to hit a pause as LLY posts its fiscal Q3 earnings on Oct. 29, according to the latest options data from Barchart.
Heading into the quarterly print, Eli Lilly stock is up more than 50% versus its year-to-date low in late April.

Consensus is for Eli Lilly to report $5.38 in earnings per share (EPS) for its third financial quarter, which would represent a more than 23% decline on a year-over-year basis.
Options traders seem to believe that would trigger a near-term selloff in LLY shares, as evidenced by the put-to-call ratio of about 2.18x on contracts expiring Nov. 6. Barchart's data also pegs the lower price on those options contracts at $1,241 as of this writing, signaling potential for a more than 3% post-earnings dip.
A small 0.54% dividend yield on the pharmaceutical behemoth nonetheless offers a reason to look beyond the near-term earnings noise.
Bernstein analysts also disagree with the options market sentiment ahead of LLY's quarterly print.
In a research note yesterday, the investment firm maintained an "Outperform" rating on the NYSE-listed giant and raised its price objective to $1,450, which signals potential upside of another 13% from here.
Bernstein's bullish thesis is rooted in better-than-expected demand for Mounjaro; analysts expect international sales of that flagship drug to grow 8% sequentially, significantly more than the 1% consensus.
Plus, Zepbound and Foundayo sales will result in upward revisions of 2027 earnings and revenue estimates, helping Eli Lilly shares rip much higher over the next 12 months, they told clients.
While not as bullish as Bernstein, other Wall Street firms are also convinced that LLY stock has more room to the upside.
The consensus rating on Eli Lilly remains at "Strong Buy," with the mean price target of about $1,363 indicating potential for an 8% rally from current levels.

Third quarter earnings season is in full swing this week, with corporate results dropping from Big Tech heavy-hitters Microsoft ( MSFT ), Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and Amazon ( AMZN ).
Read more: Follow Microsoft earnings live updates here.
Aside from Big Tech, industries from oil to chips to pharmaceuticals will be represented, as Exxon Mobil ( XOM ), Intel ( INTC ), Boeing ( BA ), Ford ( F ), and Eli Lilly ( LLY ) also open their books.
It's shaping up to be another strong earnings season. According to FactSet data , nearly a quarter of S&P 500 companies have already reported Q3 earnings so far, with an overall earnings growth rate of 29.5%. If that rate holds, it will mark the third straight quarter of earnings growth above 25%.
Crocs ( CROX ) stock soared 25% on Thursday to its highest price in over two years as investors cheered on a return to growth for the footwear company's HeyDude loafer brand and a brighter outlook for 2026 sales.
In the third quarter, HeyDude revenue increased 6.1% over the previous year to $170 million, marking the first sales increase in six quarters for the struggling shoe brand.
Crocs bought HeyDude for $2.5 billion in 2022, its largest acquisition ever. But the brand struggled amid excess inventory and discounting, causing investors to become fed up with lagging sales.
HeyDude makes up roughly 16% of Crocs' total revenue, while the flagship Crocs brand accounts for the remaining 84% of sales.
Caterpillar ( CAT ) reported and a record order backlog of $78.1 billion in the third quarter, but the stock fell 11% in premarket trading as Wall Street set a high bar and AI-related stocks broadly got hit.
The company has become a growing industrial AI play as its power generation business, which makes and services turbines, has gotten a boost amid booming data center construction.
Here's what Caterpillar reported, versus analyst estimates compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:
Revenue: increased 17% to $20.7 billion, in line with Wall Street estimates.
Adjusted earnings per share: $7.20, versus estimates of $7.03 per share.
Guidance: Maintained full-year outlook for sales to grow in the mid-to-high teens
Analysts may be down on the stock as they were hoping for raised guidance and a wider sales beat.
"Our third-quarter results reflect the durability of our end markets, with strong order rates and a record backlog," Caterpillar CEO Joe Creed said in the release. "Our team continues to execute our strategic priorities in a dynamic environment, positioning us for a strong year while delivering long-term value for our customers and shareholders."
Eli Lilly ( LLY ) shares jumped 4% in premarket trading as strong demand for the company's GLP-1 drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound boosted the company's third quarter results.
Here's what Eli Lilly reported, versus analyst estimates compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:
Revenue: up 39% year over year to $24.4 billion, versus estimates of $22.6 billion
Adjusted earnings per share: up 7% to $7.48, versus estimates of $6.35
Guidance: Increased full-year revenue guidance to a new range of $91 billion to $92 billion
"Revenue growth was driven by broad global consumer demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound, the global launches of Foundayo, expanded U.S. coverage for obesity care and a doubling in our newest products in oncology, immunology and neuroscience," Lilly CEO David Ricks said in the earnings release.
Mounjaro sales rose 65% year over year to $10.7 billion, while Zepbound sales were up 49% to $5.35 billion.
Alphabet ( GOOGL , GOOG ) profit took a hit from an unusual place: its stakes in other companies.
Those holdings include about 14% of Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) and a piece of SpaceX ( SPCX ). They supplied about $6 of Alphabet's $9.11 in per-share profit in the second quarter. In the third quarter, a nearly $9 billion loss on them cut earnings by $0.55 a share, to $2.12.
The filing that shows which stakes fell isn't out yet, but SpaceX stock dropped about 12% during the quarter.
Watch Anthropic's IPO, which could start trading as soon as Nov. 16. Once it's public, Alphabet will value that stake at the market price every quarter.
Chipotle ( CMG ) reported third quarter earnings on Wednesday after market close that were better than the Street expected as the restaurant chain sustained sales momentum following slower sales growth since the first quarter of 2025.
Chipotle posted a 2.1% gain in same-store sales, higher than the 1.5% gain Wall Street expected. It posted adjusted earnings of $0.27 per share, slightly below the $0.29 per share expected.
"Three consecutive quarters of positive comparable transaction growth demonstrates that our Recipe for Growth strategy is working," CEO Scott Boatwright wrote in the release, adding that the company saw traction around its menu and digital innovation, high-efficiency equipment rollout and global expansion.
The stock rose 2%. Year to date, shares are down 20%.
ServiceNow ( NOW ) stock plunged 15% after the company missed earnings expectations.
Here's what the enterprise software company reported in Q3, versus analyst estimates compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence:

"This was more than another beat-and-raise quarter for ServiceNow, this was the inflection point for ServiceNow as the Super Intelligence Control Tower," CEO Bill McDermott said in the earnings release. "Our customers have validated our strategic relevance as the single harness for enterprise intelligence and security."

articles.title_orig: Met refers itself to police watchdog over letter about Meghan's father
articles.title_zh: Met refers itself to police watchdog over letter about Meghan's father
articles.content_orig:
The Metropolitan Police has referred itself to the police complaints watchdog over its handling of a letter with allegations against Thomas Markle, which was handed to his daughter, the Duchess of Sussex, in 2019.
The letter, written by Markle's first wife Roslyn Loveless, is believed to have contained claims about Meghan's father.
Markle has strongly denied recent allegations that he had possessed images of child abuse, describing them as "sick lies".
The force said it had voluntarily referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) "in respect of the decision not to inform other law enforcement agencies, and the decision to pass the letter to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex."
The Met added it intended to make further referrals to "relevant overseas law enforcement agencies", a process which it expected to be completed "in the coming days".
The letter that will be considered by the IOPC was sent to the Met's royal protection team by Roslyn Loveless, who divorced Thomas Markle in 1975 and died in 2024.
The handwritten letter was then passed to Meghan in January 2019, with the duchess saying last week that it had "made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father".
Meghan did not provide any details but said it had given her sufficient reason for not visiting Thomas Markle and not allowing him to meet his grandchildren, Archie and Lilibet.
Scotland Yard said the letter contained claims about offending outside the UK and that it had been forwarded to "the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness".
Confirming that it had referred itself to the IPOC, the Metropolitan Police said it was aware of media reports that it had try to obtain a copy of the letter.
"While the letter did not actually contain any information specifically related to security matters, it did contain a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom," it said.
It added that the Met has carried out an initial review in recent days which has led to the voluntary referral to IOPC.
The watchdog will consider why the Met did not share the contents of the letter with other law enforcement agencies, in the UK or overseas, it contained claims of alleged offences.
There are also reports that the Met did not keep a copy of the letter and had to get a copy from the Sussexes.
Meghan, in a statement last week, said she believed the allegations in the letter "were being investigated".
But the watchdog will have to consider what happened to the warnings.
There are also likely to be questions about what royal officials knew about the letter, which was sent when Meghan was still a working royal, and which was forwarded to the Sussexes' office rather than to her personally.
Jim Gamble, former head of the Child Exploitation and Online Protection Centre, previously told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that he would have expected the police to have shared any warnings.
"If you get information that comes to you about someone from a foreign jurisdiction who represents a threat to children, there's a well-worn path and generally you'd expect a UK police force to share that information," said Gamble.
"I would have expected the Metropolitan Police to have gone to the FBI to say, 'Look, this isn't proven, it's an allegation, you might want to look at it'.
Noel Rasmussen, Thomas Markle's granddaughter and niece of the Duchess of Sussex, told the BBC she was "deeply troubled by the questions surrounding the Metropolitan Police's handling of the information it received".
"If allegations of this seriousness were brought to the attention of authorities, it is reasonable to ask what steps were taken, why the information was not shared with other law enforcement agencies," she said.
"I believe those questions deserve clear, transparent answers."
Reports of the Met's handline of the letter emerged as Thomas Markle's son had told the police in the Philippines about material which was alleged to contain sexual images of children, which he had claimed to have found in possessions belonging to Meghan's father.
Thomas Markle had been in the Philippines in December 2025, undergoing hospital treatment, when Meghan wrote to him to end all contact.
Authorities in the Philippines have begun investigating the claims.
Philippine Police have obtained a warrant to examine devices seized from Markle's former home.
Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old videotapes, were handed to police by Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, last week.
However, officers in Cebu needed a court warrant before they could examine the items.
Thomas Markle Sr has strongly denied all the allegations against him. He has been backed by his daughter Samantha who has dismissed the claims against her father as "fake".

articles.title_orig: U.S. economy grew at a fast clip this summer, thanks to business, consumer spending
articles.title_zh: U.S. economy grew at a fast clip this summer, thanks to business, consumer spending
articles.content_orig:
The U.S. economy grew 3.4% in the July to September quarter from a year earlier, a much faster pace of annual growth than in the second quarter. Consumer spending was one of the main drivers of growth — though many Americans continue to struggle with inflation. Joe Raedle/Getty Images North America hide caption
The U.S. economy grew faster in the summer compared to the spring, driven by consumer spending as well as investments in AI.
Gross domestic product, which broadly measures economic activity, grew at an annual rate of 3.4% July through September, according to a report from the Commerce Department released Thursday. The previous quarter GDP grew at a 2.2% annual pace.
A big driver for GDP growth in the third quarter was the strong investments from AI companies, which continue to build out data centers and spend big money in developing the technology.
Meanwhile, consumer spending was another of the big drivers of GDP growth, led in part by higher-income Americans who are better able to withstand stubbornly high inflation.
The sturdy GDP data comes just days before the midterm elections, with many Americans saying they feel gloomy about the economy as inflation jacks up the costs of many day-to-day necessities, while the ongoing conflict with Iran drives up energy costs like gasoline.
Although consumer spending has been growing steadily, it has not spread out evenly across households, with lower-income Americans struggling more than high-earners. Wage growth has also fallen behind inflation, further squeezing many Americans.
Siri Steven, a manager at a resale store in Decorah, Iowa, says she and her husband are putting off fixing up their more than 130-year-old house.
"We barely go out to eat now," Steven said. "I really have to be mindful of our budget and make sure that we can pay all our bills and not overdraft."
She also says her family hasn't been able to save, going paycheck to paycheck. The personal saving rate for the U.S. in September is 3.8%, according to a separate report from the Commerce Department, down from 4.1% in August.
Prices rose 3.6% in September from a year earlier, according to the same report, faster than the Federal Reserve's 2% target. The Fed watches the Commerce Department's inflation measure closely, particularly when deciding what to do with its benchmark interest rates.
Still, the central bank decided against raising rates Wednesday, with added pressure to raise rates during the next meeting in December after Thursday's reading on prices.
Economists also are concerned about the country's long term fiscal health. Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's Analytics, warns that despite solid GDP figures, economic growth feels delicate. That's due to business and consumers having to navigate around Trump Administration policies, such as tariffs and the U.S. war against Iran.
"We're growing," Zandi said. "The economy is moving forward but it's a very, very fragile growth. It doesn't feel like we're kicking it in on all cylinders."

articles.title_orig: Rep. Young Kim Urges Secretary Rubio to Raise China Travel Advisory to Level 3
articles.title_zh: Rep. Young Kim Urges Secretary Rubio to Raise China Travel Advisory to Level 3
articles.content_orig:
Oct 29, 2026 | Press Releases
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, House Foreign Affairs East Asia and Pacific Subcommittee Chair Young Kim (CA-40) sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the State Department to raise its travel advisory for the People’s Republic of China (PRC) from Level 2 (“Exercise Increased Caution”) to Level 3 (“Reconsider Travel”) in light of the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) ongoing wrongful detention of American citizens.
On October 19, the State Department updated its China travel advisory to warn that Americans face a serious risk of wrongful detention , arbitrary enforcement of local laws, surveillance, and illegitimate exit bans without due process. However, the advisory remains at Level 2 – the same category as allies like Italy, Germany, and the United Kingdom, where risks stem from isolated non-state threats. In China, the threat to Americans comes from the state apparatus itself, making the risk constant and countrywide.
“The United States cannot and will not tolerate a hostile foreign power treating Americans, including Mr. Min Zin and Dr. Youlin Chen, who are currently detained, like pawns to be traded,” said Rep. Young Kim. “The Chinese Communist Party continues to use hostage diplomacy as leverage against our country, and Americans considering travel to China deserve a clear, honest assessment of the risks they face. Raising the advisory to Level 3 would deliver exactly that.”
Chairwoman Kim also urged that specific cases of detained Americans, like Mr. Min Zin and Dr. Youlin Chen, be listed on the State Department’s China travel advisory webpage as a warning to Americans.
This letter builds on Chairwoman Kim’s Subcommittee hearing, “Lives Not Leverage: The Long Arm of China and North Korea’s Repression,” where she pressed for answers on whether the State Department should raise China’s travel advisory.

articles.title_orig: Ancient cosmetics, coins, mouse skeletons found in Pompeii home shed light on life before deadly eruption
articles.title_zh: Ancient cosmetics, coins, mouse skeletons found in Pompeii home shed light on life before deadly eruption
articles.content_orig:
Ancient items found in a sealed closet in Pompeii hint at what life was like in the historic Roman city before it was destroyed in the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in A.D. 79.
The closet was located in a home in the central area of the city, the Pompeii Archaeological Park said in a news release . The house had previously been excavated in 1912, but an investigation of the surrounding areas is just now underway.
Inside, archaeologists found cosmetics, an incense burner, a bronze lantern and a balsam jar. Weights, likely used for commercial activity, were also found inside a wooden chest of drawers. The researchers also found vases and pots made of materials such as bronze, glass and ceramic, and a "refined snuff bottle" decorated with pine.
A necklace representing multiple deities and made of several materials was also found. The piece of jewelry might have been considered "magical" during the Roman era, the park said. Now these pieces are known as "crepundia," or rattles. The necklaces have amulets, meant to protect the wearer as a child. Many carried them into adulthood as mementos of childhood, the park said.
There were high levels of "geographical mobility" in the Roman world, the archaeological park said, explaining that many people, from slaves to wealthy merchants, lived far from relatives and the places they were raised.
The necklace found in the closet contains at least 20 miniature objects and materials including bone and crystal.
The wardrobe also held 38 bronze coins, preserved in a container made of plant material. The presence of the coins has led researchers to believe that the owner or owners didn't have time to recover valuable items.
It's impossible to know what happened to the people who owned these items, the archaeological park said. They may have escaped the eruption of Vesuvius and been unable to return to the site and dig for their belongings. They may have died in the disaster, along with about 15% to 20% of Pompeii's population , or afterward, without heirs who could reclaim the objects.
Little is known about the residents of the house. The items in the closet, including the paintings, and the location of the home on one of Pompeii's main streets suggest "a certain standard of living." But mouse skeletons found inside the home cast some doubt on this belief. However, such skeletons have been found in other spots of Pompeii, showing the city contended with "unwelcome guests," the park said.
The home has previously been attributed to a person named Cornelius Maximus, the archaeological park said. That identification was based on the discovery of inscriptions that are no longer visible. The newly found items likely won't bring researchers closer to identifying the home's owner, but they allow archaeologists to study "the various traces of a life," said archaeological park director Gabriel Zuchtriegel in the Facebook post.
"We cannot reconstruct with certainty the identity of those who lived in the house, but these fragments bring us closer to their daily lives," said Zuchtriegel.
Pompeii is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site and popular tourist attraction. Archaeologists are also constantly exploring the ruined city, searching under heaps of volcanic ash and pumice to peer into its preserved remains.
In January, the archaeological park announced that researchers had found a 2,000-year-old love note and illustrated gladiator fight scene inscribed on a city wall. In December 2025, archaeologists found evidence suggesting that some Pompeii residents returned to live in the city after the eruption.

articles.title_orig: Pentagon says Iran war has cost US taxpayers $47bn: What that means
articles.title_zh: Pentagon says Iran war has cost US taxpayers $47bn: What that means
articles.content_orig:
The Pentagon has told lawmakers in the United States that the war on Iran has cost American taxpayers at least $47.1bn so far.
The estimate, disclosed last week, comes days before Tuesday’s midterm elections, which will determine if President Donald Trump’s Republican Party will maintain control of Congress for the next two years.
In a statement on Wednesday the Pentagon said it had “successfully obligated 97.5 percent” of the funds Trump provided the department. In July last year, Trump signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBA) outlining tax and spending plans that came into effect this year.
We take a close look at the Pentagon’s estimate, and what it means for the US economy and the midterm elections.
The Pentagon told Congress that the cost of the US-Israel war on Iran as of October 16 had risen to at least $47.1bn.
Congressional officials shared the Pentagon’s cost estimate breakdown with The New York Times.
According to the Times and other US media, the Pentagon’s estimate covers the operational costs of the war and includes a projected cost of $29bn needed to replace expended munitions such as bombs, bullets and other military hardware that has been deployed in the war so far.
It also reveals that since the war started on February 28, the US Air Force has spent $7.6bn on fighter and bomber units, the US Navy has spent $1.5bn on two dozen warships and aircraft carriers and the US Army has spent $2.1bn to sustain its troops in the Middle East.
According to the US military’s Central Command, there are more than 50,000 American soldiers stationed in the Middle East, comprising personnel deployed to large, permanent bases and to smaller forward sites across the region.
Officials told the Times that the Pentagon has spent $6.1bn to replace damaged aircraft and munitions, $645m on transport and support for commandos in the region and $24.5m on “in-house medical support” for US service members.
A congressional official added that the US Transportation Command also spent $92.2m to move equipment and the US Cyber Command spent $14m on “cyber support operations”.
The Pentagon’s estimate, however, does not include how much Washington will need to spend to repair its military bases across the Middle East that were damaged in Iranian attacks and also does not take into account the cost of fuel to power ships and aircraft used in the war.
While the Pentagon has publicly acknowledged 18 US service member fatalities in the war, The Washington Post has cited six unnamed US officials stating the true death toll is at least 22. According to the official Pentagon Defense Casualty Analysis System (DCAS) database, 865 military personnel have been wounded in the war with Iran.
John Phillips, a British safety, security and risk adviser and a former military chief instructor, told Al Jazeera that the Pentagon’s $47.1bn estimate should be treated as a running total and not the total cost of the war.
“If the war continues without a durable outcome, the US risks paying repeatedly to sustain military pressure while simultaneously trying to rebuild the capability it has consumed,” he said.
He said that replacing advanced weapons also requires industrial capacity and time and that money and production resources committed to this conflict may also compete with other defence priorities.
“What concerns me most is the possibility of an open-ended commitment: continuing to spend heavily without a clear political end state or a settlement that delivers lasting security,” he said.
Currently, the US must weigh three costs, Phillips said: the money spent, the military capability consumed and the economic disruption generated.
“A tactical victory is not necessarily a strategic victory. If the conflict leaves US stockpiles depleted, energy markets unstable and regional security unresolved, the question is not simply how much the war will cost but whether its lasting benefits justify the price,” he said.
According to an October 19 report by USA Today, five senators from the Democratic Party had written to Admiral Brad Cooper, the head of Central Command, demanding that the Pentagon reveal the true cost of the war. Their letter said the Trump administration’s “ongoing efforts to hide the true cost of this war are outrageous and unacceptable”.
Trump has not commented on the latest Pentagon estimate. But the Trump administration’s war on Iran has grown increasingly unpopular with US citizens due to its impact on US and global energy costs.
Since early March, shortly after the war began, Iran has closed the critical Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf, through which about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies were shipped until then. This has sent the price of oil spiralling and caused shortages globally. In the US, diesel, which is heavily relied on by farmers and small businesses, has nearly doubled in price.
In a post on X following the latest Pentagon report, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York wrote: “For eight months, American families have been buried by the heavy cost of Trump’s disastrous war in Iran.
“Trump and his ego led us into this war with no plan, no authority, and no exit strategy,” he added.
Estimates for the cost of the Iran war to the US have risen steadily as the war has continued.
The Pentagon’s latest estimate is higher than the $38bn the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) forecast in September.
It is also higher than the $37.5bn price tag that US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth gave in July this year. Hegseth confirmed this amount during a hearing before the Senate appropriations committee and added that the cost covered some operations and maintenance extending through to the end of September.
Hegseth’s July estimate was already about $8bn higher than the previous figure released by the Trump administration in May – $29bn.
Prior to the May estimate, in late April the Pentagon’s comptroller Jules Hurst reported that the war would cost $25bn.
Meanwhile, with the war entering its ninth month and no peace deal in sight, last month the CBO said the war with Iran could cost approximately $2bn to $3bn per month for as long as it continues.
The Pentagon’s inspector general also said last month that US troops are facing “strategic inventory shortfalls” as the war continues.
But the Trump administration has denied it is running low on weapons stockpiles.
“Cowards and traitors would like to say that the United States is short of ammunition, but that is not true. We have more ammunition than we could ever imagine using. And we are producing it at levels we have never reached before,” Trump told the United Nations General Assembly in New York in September.
Trump has also repeatedly stated that the Iran war will end when he wants it to.
Last week at an election rally in Texas, according to a report by CNBC, Trump said: “Somebody asked me before, ‘When will the war in Iran end?’ I said, ‘Whenever I want it to end.’”
The US-Israel war on Iran has affected the US economy through direct government spending as well as rising energy and fuel costs.
On Wednesday, the average price of a gallon of diesel in the US hit $6.35, compared with $3.75 last year, according to the American Automobile Association.
Higher fuel costs are also driving up the cost of food – with shortages of oil and gas affecting nearly every stage of the food supply chain.
Meanwhile, the country’s national debt has surpassed a record $40 trillion, two years before expected.
As a result, the war has become deeply unpopular in the US and Trump’s approval ratings have slumped to just 33 percent – the lowest they have been at any time during his two terms as president.
With five days to go before the midterms, analysts say confirmation by the Pentagon of the high cost of the war is likely to affect how people in the US vote.
Currently, the Democrats lead Republicans by 51.4 percent to 43.2 percent, a gap of 8.2 percentage points, according to RealClearPolling’s national polling average.
Chris

articles.title_orig: Nasdaq falls as Alphabet set for record loss amid AI spending woes
articles.title_zh: Nasdaq falls as Alphabet set for record loss amid AI spending woes
articles.content_orig:
Alphabet shares were down sharply following the opening bell on Thursday while Microsoft traded largely flat as investors focused on the tech giants' latest spending and free cash flow numbers in their third-quarter earnings.
Alphabet plummeted 12% in morning trading while Microsoft was little changed.
If Alphabet closes more than 9.77% lower on Thursday, it would be its worst post-earnings reaction ever. The company went public in 2004.
Microsoft reported $45.2 billion in capital expenditures and finance leases during the third quarter, which was 30% higher than a year ago, but below analyst projections of $50.67 billion. Free cash flow fell 27% to $18.63 billion but remained positive.
Alphabet, in contrast, reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion for the third quarter, which fell much further than the $2.70 billion analysts expected by analysts. The Google parent maintained its full year capital expenditure guidance of between $195 billion and $205 billion.
The earnings report comes as investors scrutinize AI spending plans of tech companies and are focusing on the returns on those investments.
"Microsoft is building out its architecture in a measured way and as such contains fewer surprises," Ben Barringer, global head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot, said on Thursday.
"Alphabet, by contrast, saw its share price hit after hours as a result of a fairly messy set of results and a poorly handled earnings call," Barringer added.
Alphabet's biggest source of revenue, search advertising, grew 12% in the September quarter to $63.35 billion, but missed analyst expectations, adding further pressure to the company's shares.
Philipp Schindler, Alphabet's chief business officer, said the impact on the search business was partly because of lower monetization within the company's AI Mode. He added that Alphabet is now "scaling" ads within its AI Overviews and AI Mode products, including in international markets.
Google's search business has faced headwinds from the rise of other AI chatbots like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude. People may be carrying out more search queries outside Google. Gemini, Google's own AI chatbot, has failed to keep pace.
"The problem for Google is it faces an innovator's dilemma and doesn't know whether to protect its core business or look to join the disruption. As such, Google has lost its edge with Gemini and is behind peers on agentic AI," Barringer said.
Google's dominant market share in the search business, however, could ultimately give it a leg up over its peers, Rosenblatt Securities analyst Scott Devitt said.
"I don't think it's a sea change," Devitt told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Thursday. "If it's a problem for Alphabet, it's a problem for any consumer-facing AI agent or LLM as well. And so, it's a problem that I think is ultimately going to be resolved. And when it does, Alphabet, with its 4 billion search customers that become AI customers, is in an enviable position."
- CNBC's Robert Hum, Samantha Subin, Jordan Novet and Caleigh Keating contributed reporting.

A top executive of a Singapore AI cloud firm that was accused of illegally selling Nvidia chips to China could also have been a Chinese spy, anonymous sources told the New York Times .
